div.head: III Eg 3
div.ab: ⁊ se dema, se ðe oðrum on woh gedeme, gesylle þam cynge hundtwelfti scill' to bote — butan he mid aðe gecyðan durre, þæt he hit na rihtor ne cuðe — ⁊ þolige á his þegnscipes, butan he hine eft æt þam cynge gebigge, swa he him geðafian wille; ⁊ ámanige þære scyr biscop þa bote to ðæs cynges handa.

⁊ se déma, þe oðrum woh deme, gesylle þam cinge hundtwelftig scill' to bote — butan he mid aðe cyþan durre, þæt he hit na rihtor ne cuðe — ⁊ ðolige áa his ðegnscypes, butan he hine æt þam cynge gebicge, swa swa he him geðafian wille; ⁊ amanige þære scyre bisceop þa bote to ðæs cynges handa.

⁊ se dema, þe oðrum woh déme, gesille þam cynge hundtwelftig scill' to bote — buton he mid aðe gecyðan durre, þæt he hit na rihtor ne cuðe — ⁊ þolige áá his þegenscipes, buton he hine æt ðam cynge gebicge, swa he him geþafian wille; ⁊ ofmanige scirebiscop þa bote to ðæs cynges handa.

. . . twelftig scill' to bote — butan he hit mid aðe gecyþan durre, þæt he hit na rihtor ne cuðe — ⁊ þolie áá his þegenscipes, butan he hine æt þam cynge gebicge, swa he him þafian wille; ⁊ ofmanige þære scire biscop þa bote to ðæs cynges handa.
Et iudex qui iudicium iniustum iudicabit alicui, det regi CXX sol., nisi iurare audeat, quod rectius nesciuit; et admanniat scyre presul emendam illam ad manum regis.

[Be unrihtum dome.] ⁊ se dema, þe oðrum woh deme, gesille þam cynge hundtwelftig scill' to bote—buton he mid aðe gecyðan durre, þæt he hit na rihtor ne cuðe—⁊ þolige áá his þegenscipes, buton he hine æt ðam cynge gebicge, swa he him geþafian wille; ⁊ ofmanige scirebiscop þa bote to ðæs cynges handa.

And se dema, se ðe oðrum on woh gedeme, gesylle þam cynge hundtwelfti scillinga to bote—butan he mid aðe gecyðan durre þæt he hit na rihtor ne cuðe—and þolige a his þegnscipes, butan he hine eft æt þam cynge gebigge, swa he him geðafian wille; and amanige þære scyre biscop þa bote to ðæs cynges handa.

(Von ungerechtem Urtheil. Ld). Und der Richter, welcher jemandem (in G) Ungerechtigkeit zuerkennt, zahle dem König 120 Schilling als Busse — ausser wenn er durch Eid zu beweisen wagt, dass er es nicht richtiger wusste —, und verliere immer seine Thegnwürde [sammt Gerichtshoheit], ausser wenn er sie (wieder G) vom Könige auslöst, so wie dieser ihm zu gestatten geruht; und es fordere der Diöcesanbischof diese Busse zu des Königs Gunsten ein.

(Of unjust judgment. Ld) And the judge who awards injustice to another (in, G) [judgment], let him pay the king 120 shillings as compensation — unless he dares to declare on oath that he did not know how to do it more justly — and let him lose his thegnly rank [together with his jurisdiction] for ever, unless he buys it back (again, G) from the king, as the king is willing to permit him; and let the bishop of the shire exact the compensation on the king's behalf.

And a judge who gives a false judgment against another man shall pay 120 shillings as compensation to the king, unless he is prepared to declare on oath that he did not know how to give a more just decision; and he shall forfeit for ever his rank as a thegn, unless he redeem it from the king on such terms as the king will allow him. And the bishop of the diocese shall exact the compensation on the king's behalf.

And the judge who pronounces a wrong judgment on another is to pay to the king 120 shillings as compensation, unless he dare declare on oath that he knew not how to do it more justly- and he is always to forfeit his thegnly status, unless he may redeem it from the king, according as he will allow him. And the bishop of the diocese is to exact the compensation on the king’s behalf.

And a judge who rules unjustly against another must give one hundred twenty shillings to the king as compensation—unless he is confident enough to declare on oath that he did not know how to rule more justly—and forfeit forever his status as thane, unless he redeems it from the king in such a manner as the latter will permit him; and the bishop of the diocese shall exact the fine on the king’s behalf.
div.note: G2 (Nero A I f. 89, c. 1060) begins here at ‘…twelftig scill’ to bote’. Liebermann compares II As 25.1. G2 is in another hand than G and was originally a separate part of the manuscript; Liebermann prints it as a fourth column to the end of III Eg (pp. 201–207).

Unter dem Richter (s. d. Gl 3) ist zunächst an den königlichen Gerichtsvogt, bes. den Sheriff, gedacht. Denn die Busse für solch Amtsvergehen fordert der Bischof doch nur mangels des königlichen Beamten ein. Vom privaten Gerichtsherrn würde sie der Fiskalvogt eintreiben. Doch ist ausdrücklich bei Benutzern Eg's (franchise Leis Wl 39) der mit privater Gerichtsbarkeit (s. d. Gl 11b. f. 33-d) Privilegierte mitgemeint; und so schon von Eg, laut der Parallele IV As 7 = III Em 7, 2; sonst würde Eg nicht den Verlust von þegnscipe androhen, sondern von scir oder gerefscipe.

By the judge (see that word in Gl 3) is meant in the first place the king’s reeve of justice, esp. the sheriff. For the bishop, after all, exacts the compensation for such official misconduct only in default of the royal officer. From a private lord of jurisdiction the fiscal reeve would collect it. But those who used Eg (franchise Leis Wl 39) expressly include also the man privileged with private jurisdiction (see that word in Gl 11b. f. 33-d); and so did Eg himself, as the parallel IV As 7 = III Em 7, 2 shows; otherwise Eg would threaten the loss not of þegnscipe but of scir or gerefscipe.
G's on scheint auch Q nicht vorgelegen, also dem Archetyp, wie in AD, gefehlt zu haben
G’s on seems not to have been before Q either, and thus to have been lacking in the archetype, as in AD
Falsches Urteil (s. d. Gl 1a—2) wird von der Krone benutzt, um Entscheidungen aus den Niedergerichten an sich zu ziehen; Pol Mai II 664
False judgment (see that word in Gl 1a—2) is used by the Crown to draw decisions away from the lower courts to itself; Pol Mai II 664
Also nur ‘Ungehorsam’; s. d. Gl 6; strenger anderswo
Thus only ‘disobedience’; see that word in Gl 6; stricter elsewhere
Auch diese Amtsentsetzung (s. d. Gl 4. 6. 10. 11) trifft, wie das Strafgeld, vielleicht nicht das gutgläubige falsche Urteil
This removal from office (see that word in Gl 4. 6. 10. 11), like the fine, perhaps does not apply either to a false judgment given in good faith

Eg versteht unter þegnscipe auch IV 2a politische Berechtigung, nicht bloss Adel samt persönlichem Ansehen. Sachlich also richtig setzt dafür þegnscipes et iudiciaria dignitate Hn 34; nur dignitas sagt er 13; und mit dignitas übertragen Q und Consil die entsprechende Stelle in Cnut, weniger erschöpfend liberalitas Inst.—Vgl. Gl Begnadigung 8 C

By þegnscipe Eg means, in IV 2a too, political entitlement, not merely nobility together with personal standing. Hn 34 is therefore correct in substance in putting þegnscipes et iudiciaria dignitate for it; in 13 he says only dignitas; and Q and Consil render the corresponding passage in Cnut with dignitas, Inst less exhaustively with liberalitas. — Cf. Gl Begnadigung 8 C
Für ofmanian gibt Toller keinen weiteren Beleg
Toller gives no further instance of ofmanian

Liebermann is of opinion that the judge referred to is primarily the royal official (i.e. in most cases the sheriff), otherwise the duty of exacting the compensation would not fall upon the bishop. He points out, however, that in Leis Wl. 39, 1, where this law of Edgar’s is repeated, the punishment threatened is loss of franchise, i.e. the right of holding a court, and in view of the fact that the penalty mentioned by Edgar is loss of þegnscipe not of scir or gerefscipe concludes that those with the privilege of exercising private jurisdiction are likewise thought of in both cases.

note.label: status
note.seg: literally, “his thegnship”, which normally means “the rank and privileges of a thegn”. This word was probably chosen here instead of folgað “office”, as a term which could apply to holders of private jurisdictions as well as appointed officials.
